deposits.notes: Third-party resource cited in Appendix A.1, footnotes 6 and 7 (p. 13), for the Organisciak classifier, prior human ideas, and seed materials. The README identifies this as materials for Organisciak et al., Beyond Semantic Distance: Automated Scoring of Divergent Thinking Greatly Improves with Large Language Models, not a deposit of the c002 experiment. Both paper links returned HTTP 200: https://github.com/massivetexts/llm_aut_study/blob/main/notebooks/Process_AUT_GT.ipynb and https://github.com/massivetexts/llm_aut_study/blob/main/results/evaluation.zip. The recursive GitHub tree API returned HTTP 200, truncated=false, with 12 file blobs at HEAD bb952606c4167c4352c8240b7d02b88af3e6d669. Downloaded results/evaluation.zip in memory from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/massivetexts/llm_aut_study/main/results/evaluation.zip (HTTP 200; 3560943 bytes; 55 non-directory archive members). The paper's gt_main2/gpt-ft-davinci-1.csv is inside evaluation/gt_main2/. This file has 3030 rows, 1384 distinct participant values, and columns: [empty index header], id, model, participant, prompt, target, predicted, src, total_tokens, proportion. All 3030 rows have predicted values. It does not contain response text or the five c002 conditions. rows_checked and columns_checked below refer to evaluation/gt_main2/SemDis_TASA_nf_m.csv: 3030 rows, 1384 distinct participant values, nonempty response texts, and 3030 matching id values with the Davinci scores file. Also inspected evaluation/gt_byprompt/SemDis_TASA_nf_m.csv: 3390 rows, 819 distinct participant values, the same columns as the SemDis gt_main2 file, and response texts. The source values in gt_main2 are betal18, bs12, dod20, hmsl, motesf, motesp, setal08, snb17, and snbmo09. These are prior AUT studies. No S1 arm assignment, chain/trial identifiers, or S1 participant responses were identified. S2 uses a random sample of prior human ideas plus newly generated ChatGPT ideas; the actual selected sample and those ChatGPT stimuli were not identified here. studies_covered is therefore unclear rather than claiming coverage of S1 or S2. has_outcome_scores and has_texts_or_ideas describe the upstream data actually inspected, not c002 participants. The notebook describes some original MOTES data as obtainable by request; that statement concerns a different study and does not establish on-request access to c002. No requests were made. LICENSE and README were read from raw.githubusercontent.com (HTTP 200). LICENSE is MIT, copyright 2022 DU Massive Texts Lab; no separate data-specific license was identified.

Cited at p. 29, SI 11.2, footnote 9, as the source of the banned-word list used for content moderation. The repository web page, recursive tree API, raw README, and raw LICENSE returned HTTP 200. The complete current tree contains 31 file blobs (truncated=false; HEAD 0ae3460863120bc671361b9403cc65d5f2075b89), including word lists and filtering code. It contains no experiment responses, participant identifiers, outcome scores, or assignment data. S1 coverage denotes a methodological input only. The July 8, 2023 snapshot and the two additional words described in the paper were not verified. The MIT license names Robert James Gabriel / Coffee & Fun LLC.

notes: Checked on 2026-10-09. Read all 1169 lines of the markdown conversion, including references, Appendices A-D, and Supplementary Information SI 1-SI 11; checked relevant PDF text and link annotations across the 29-page PDF. The saved paper is arXiv:2401.13481v3, 31 July 2025, DOI 10.1145/3715928.3737481. The arXiv landing page returned HTTP 200 and identifies v3 as the latest version. The document ends mid-sentence in SI 11.3. No availability statement, preregistration, or repository for this paper's own experiment data or analysis code was found. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty. The statements below include provenance and materials/software references; none promises public or on-request access to the S1 data. Quotes are extracted from the PDF, with line wrapping, line-end word hyphenation, and broken URLs normalized. Overall status code_or_materials_only refers to resources available for c002: classifier/seed materials and a moderation word list. The upstream classifier repository does contain older output-level human data, but those are not c002 randomized-study observations. Therefore it does not establish public_participant_data or public_partial for S1. No public c002 data were confirmed that would support per-person or per-arm means, SDs, SEs, analyzed participant counts, or participant/chain-aware diversity estimates. In final.open_items, the missing per-arm counts, unexplained gap between 3414 retained responses and the 3271/2618 model observations, and absence of participant-level uncertainty for diversity remain unresolved. The old classifier data cannot recover the c002 model samples or resolve the disclosure/global-diversity discrepancies. Publisher checks: https://doi.org/10.1145/3715928.3737481 returned HTTP 403, and https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715928.3737481 returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot-check page. Stopped there. Separate publisher supplementary files could not be inspected; a bot check does not establish that a dataset requires an account or is unavailable. This limitation is why confidence is medium. The publisher page and arXiv article are not counted as data deposits. Other paper links checked with urllib: https://www.mindgarden.com/67-alternate-uses (p. 3, footnote 1), HTTP 200, commercial AUT test information; https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/emmeans/index.html (p. 8, footnote 5), HTTP 200, general R-package documentation; https://www.creativemornings.com/ (p. 4, footnote 4), HTTP 202 with an empty response body, recruitment organization; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 (p. 1), HTTP 200, article-license terms. These are not deposits of c002 data. All network requests used User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 without email or personal identifiers; no login, account creation, access request, or bot-check circumvention was attempted. Only the two repositories explicitly named in the paper were queried through the GitHub API (one recursive-tree request each). Downloaded resources were examined in memory. Negative searches mean no relevant deposit was identified within the checked sources, not proof that none exists.

corrections.basis: Both posted-data analysts (analysis/c002/A.json and B.json, 2026-10-10) found that this repository is the Organisciak classifier-validation dataset that the paper cites for its originality scorer (Appendix A.1, PDF p. 13, footnotes 6-7): its 55 CSV files hold earlier AUT benchmark scores, not this paper's randomized experiment. None of the paper's printed statistics could be reproduced from it.
